analysis.title: GS 2027 Outlooks / Global Equity Outlook / Global Macro Outlook / Nvidia / Siemens / Semicon Takes / Ottobock / Zealand / Global Transport / Europe Banks Tracker
key_insights: GS Global Equity Strategy 2027 Outlook: earnings growth is on course to slow sharply across all major regions in 2027, growth in AI capex is likely to peak, and the cost of capital remains elevated.

GS expects equities to keep rising in 2027 but with high volatility, citing sharp de-rating, more attractive valuations, positive but slower nominal economic and earnings growth, and lower bond yields, inflation and oil prices.
GS equity positioning for 2027: Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower bond yields.

GS Macro Outlook 2027 (Steady Baseline, Downside Risks): two more Fed hikes and one ECB hike expected, with both returning to cuts in late 2027. Most GS forecasts for other central banks are below market pricing.
GS expects longer-term rates to come down modestly despite large government deficits and heavy AI-linked borrowing.

GS expects positive returns for equities and bonds in 2027 but a bumpy path. The AI investment boom has had a much larger impact on earnings and market values than on GDP growth, and markets may worry whether the record share of GDP going to US earnings can persist as the capex impulse peaks.
If AI capex still rises strongly in 2027, positive earnings growth should cushion the transition, but ongoing financing needs will likely keep pushing credit spreads wider.

Nvidia (NVDA): GS views the announced management transition as fluid with possibly more information to come, but expects a measured direct impact on financials and earnings power over the next 12-18 months, given a 12-24 month backlog and order book and a clearly defined 2-3 year product roadmap already in execution.
Siemens AG after 4Q26: the CEO and CFO met the sell side in London. GS concluded Siemens has had a strong start to fiscal FY27 in automation, with double-digit software growth expected for the year.
Siemens: data center growth visibility remains strong despite potential near-term order volatility and supply-chain dynamics.

Siemens: the company intends to maintain M&A discipline while prioritizing software assets, particularly in building services, plus selective hardware. Mobility is core to its AI strategy, with greater platform conformity enforced to protect segment margins.
SEMICON Europa (Munich, 11 Nov): GS met VAT Group, Ebara, Pfeiffer Vacuum, Inficon and Edwards Vacuum (Atlas Copco's VT division). The detailed takeaways are not in this summary.

Ottobock (OBCK.DE): GS reiterates Buy and sees the sharp underperformance after Q3 26 results as overdone, with reimbursement uncertainty in focus. Core revenue/EBITDA/EPS estimates are cut by 0-6% across FY26/27/28e and the 12-month target price falls to €65 from €75.
Ottobock: GS says management needs to specify what the reimbursement challenges are and whether they are transitory or structural, and to deliver consistent, predictable performance.
Zealand Pharma (ZELA.CO) 3Q26 review: glepaglutide EU approval is the near-term catalyst, and obesity newsflow is quieter for now.
Also listed by title only, with no content in this document: 'Around the World in 80 Charts' on tracking the US import cycle, and a Europe Banks earnings tracker covering ABN, KBC and UCG.
